description: Dex Agents CLI configuration behavior every CLI core must match: YAML parsing, schema validation, file defaults, the Dex server's authentication and TLS settings, the media store, remote MCP servers and their header variables, session override narrowing, operation names, and the shell allow list. Hand-written; see README.md and agents/cli/README.md.

error_codes.yaml: The file is not one YAML 1.2 document with unique keys. path is always "".
error_codes.schema: The value fails the schema. CLI cores may report schema errors in any order. Each schema case has exactly one violation, and a CLI core passes it when validation fails and the expected instance location path and keyword are among its validator's errors, nested anyOf errors included.
error_codes.invalid_url: dex.server, dex.auth.token_url, connectors.mcp, media.endpoint, or an mcp_servers URL passes the schema but is not a URL a WHATWG URL parser accepts with a port of at most 65535: an IPv4 part that is not 0 or a decimal from 1 to 255 without a leading zero, an invalid IPv6 address, a DNS label starting with xn--, or a port over 65535. path is the field.
error_codes.insecure_token_url: dex.auth.token_url is an http URL whose host is not loopback: localhost in any case, an IPv4 address in 127.0.0.0/8, or the IPv6 address ::1 in any spelling. path is "/dex/auth/token_url".
error_codes.insecure_mcp_server_url: An mcp_servers URL is an http URL whose host is not loopback, by the rule of insecure_token_url. path is "/mcp_servers/<name>/url".
error_codes.literal_credential_header: An mcp_servers header whose name is credential-like, by the credential_names rule of approval_display.json, has no ${NAME} reference in its value. path is "/mcp_servers/<name>/headers/<header>".
error_codes.auth_needs_server_url: dex.auth.mode is not none, but dex.server is auto or omitted: the local dexcli dev takes no credential. path is "/dex/auth".
error_codes.tls_needs_https_server: dex.tls sets ca_file or server_name, but dex.server is not an https URL. An empty dex.tls passes. path is "/dex/tls".
error_codes.duplicate_tool: One entry names the same operation twice, in two spellings. path is the entry.
error_codes.duplicate_connection: Two entries cover the same connection. path is the later entry.
error_codes.model_required: Neither the file nor the harness command gives a model.
error_codes.widens_connectors: A session entry is not inside any entry of the file. path is the entry.
error_codes.widens_local_tools: A session switches on what the file switches off, or allows a command the file does not.
error_codes.unsupported_reasoning_effort: A session's reasoning_effort passes the schema but is not one of the values the harness command declares, or the command declares none. path is "/reasoning_effort".

warnings: Resolving session settings also returns warnings: the JSON Pointer of every top-level key the session settings schema does not define, sorted by key in Unicode code point order. Those keys are ignored. Settings that fail resolution report no warnings. A TypeScript CLI core must compare code points: the default Array sort compares UTF-16 code units and puts U+10000 before U+E000.
check_order: Report the first failure in this order: yaml; schema; invalid_url for dex.server, then dex.auth.token_url, then connectors.mcp, then media.endpoint, then each mcp_servers URL; then insecure_token_url; then insecure_mcp_server_url for each mcp_servers URL; then literal_credential_header for each mcp_servers header; then auth_needs_server_url; then tls_needs_https_server; then connector entries in list order, each checked for duplicate_tool, duplicate_connection against earlier entries, and (sessions only) widens_connectors; then model_required; then local_tools in the order files, shell.enabled, shell.allow by index, web_fetch, browser; then, for sessions only, reasoning_effort against the harness command's values. The mcp_servers checks take the servers in Unicode code point order of their names, and a server's headers in Unicode code point order of their names.

dex_connection.description: How a CLI core turns a valid file's dex section and its environment into the Dex connection settings: TLS, and how to authenticate, without any secret. The file's dex.auth.mode alone turns authentication on; the variables never do. Every variable is trimmed, and one that is empty after trimming is not set. A variable overrides the matching field of the selected mode: DEX_TOKEN_URL, DEX_SERVER_ID, and DEX_CREDENTIAL_FILE. DEX_TLS_CA_FILE and DEX_TLS_SERVER_NAME override dex.tls, and are read only for an https dex.server. DEX_TLS and DEX_FLOW_SERVICE_ADDRESS are never read. A file path from the configuration file expands a leading ~ to home and is otherwise relative to the configuration file's directory; a path from a variable expands ~ the same way and is otherwise relative to working_directory. Paths are normalized lexically, without reading the file system. A DEX_TOKEN_URL passes the token_url pattern of the configuration schema and the invalid_url and insecure_token_url checks. The checks run in this order and the first failure is the error: for api_key, the token URL (DEX_TOKEN_URL is checked when it is set), the server ID, then DEX_API_KEY; for bearer env, DEX_CREDENTIAL; for bearer file, the path. An error names the one setting to fix and its message is exact. The settings never hold a secret: auth is the launch document's dex.auth, with the token file's path in file for bearer file.

mcp_servers.description: How a CLI core turns a valid file's mcp_servers and its environment into the servers its Worker connects to. Each ${NAME} reference in a header value is replaced by the value of the environment variable NAME, exactly as set, without trimming; the result is never expanded again, and any other $ stays as written. A variable that is not set or is empty, or whose value has a character outside printable ASCII (U+0020 to U+007E), is an error that names the setting and the variable and never the value. The servers come in Unicode code point order of their names. The checks take the servers in that order, the headers of a server in Unicode code point order of their names, and the references of a value from left to right; the first failure is the error, and its message is exact. Only the Worker expands the values, when the command starts: the effective configuration, the session, and every log keep the text as written.
